source_fields.formulation: The learner faces multiple reward objectives ordered by priority. Each round selects one arm and observes its complete reward vector. The comparator is the lexicographically optimal arm. Known tradeoff coefficients control improvements in lower-priority objectives relative to losses in higher-priority ones; performance is retained as signed regret for each objective.
source_fields.solution_goal: Minimize performance as defined by the metric, guarantee, and native resource.

source_fields.instance: The finite action set has $K$ arms with a discrete metric of diameter at most $1$. Each arm has $m$ fixed mean rewards $\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_m$, ordered by priority, and each mean function is $1$-Lipschitz. Each objective has oscillation at most $1$; irrelevant common additive shifts are unrestricted. A lexicographically optimal arm $x^\star$ exists. Ties are allowed: each lower-priority objective is compared among arms optimal for all higher priorities. The tradeoff coefficient must be finite: $$\lambda_\star=\inf\!\left\{\lambda\ge0:\ \mu_i(x)-\mu_i(x^\star)\le\lambda\max_{j<i}\bigl(\mu_j(x^\star)-\mu_j(x)\bigr),\ \forall x\in\mathcal X,\ 2\le i\le m\right\}<\infty.$$

operations.query_signature: Choose an arm $x_t$ and then observe all $m$ reward coordinates. Conditional on the past and current arm, each coordinate is $1$-sub-Gaussian around its fixed mean; coordinates need not be independent. $$\mathbb E\!\left[e^{s(Y_{t,i}-\mu_i(x_t))}\mid\mathcal H_{t-1},x_t\right]\le e^{s^2/2}\qquad(s\in\mathbb R,\ 1\le i\le m).$$ Causal randomized policies are allowed. Inputs $K,m,T,\delta_{\mathrm{conf}}$ and a tradeoff bound satisfying $\lambda\ge\lambda_\star$ are public. Mean vectors and the set of primary-objective optimal arms are hidden. Observed feedback may be stored and reused computationally; no unrevealed past information or additional queries to exhausted samples are available. Any within-round full-function or common-sample access must be explicit.

model.instance: The public action set is $\mathcal X=[K]$ with $K\ge2$ and the discrete metric $D(x,y)=\mathbf1\{x\ne y\}$. There are exactly two fixed mean functions $\mu^1,\mu^2$, each 1-Lipschitz in D and each with oscillation at most one. Common additive offsets may differ between the two coordinates and are unrestricted; the gaps, local tradeoff, and regret are invariant under these offsets. The primary optimum set is $\mathcal X_1^*=\operatorname{argmax}_{x\in\mathcal X}\mu^1(x)$, and a lexicographic optimum $x^*\in\operatorname{argmax}_{x\in\mathcal X_1^*}\mu^2(x)$ exists. Primary ties are permitted. The finite local tradeoff is $\lambda_*=\inf\{b\ge0:\mu^2(x)-\mu^2(x^*)\le b[\mu^1(x^*)-\mu^1(x)]\ \forall x\in\mathcal X\}$. A finite upper bound $\lambda\ge\lambda_*\ge0$ is supplied to the policy.

The primary optimum set is $\mathcal X_1^*=\operatorname{argmax}_{x\in\mathcal X}\mu^1(x)$, and a lexicographic optimum $x^*\in\operatorname{argmax}_{x\in\mathcal X_1^*}\mu^2(x)$ exists. Primary ties are permitted.

operations.query_signature: At round t, choose one arm $X_t\in\mathcal X$ using past observations and independent internal randomness, then receive both coordinates $(Y_t^1,Y_t^2)$. Conditional on the past and current arm, $\mathbb E[\exp(\theta(Y_t^i-\mu^i(X_t)))\mid\mathcal H_{t-1},X_t]\le\exp(\theta^2/2)$ for all real theta and i=1,2. Cross-coordinate independence is not required. No unselected-arm feedback, same-round second pull, or historical requery is provided. Public inputs are K,T, the fact m=2, and the finite supplied upper bound lambda. No external confidence parameter is required by this expected-regret view. Mean functions, the primary-optimal arm set, and the lexicographic optimum are hidden.

metric.normalization: Cumulative regret is not divided by T. Compute each coordinate expectation separately and then take their maximum. No positive part or reward scalarization is applied.
metric.finiteness_conditions: Each coordinate mean has oscillation at most one and T is finite, so -T<=R_i(T)<=T, R_1(T)>=0, and 0<=max_i E[R_i(T)]<=T.
description_paragraphs: Define $R_i(T)=\sum_t[\mu^i(x^*)-\mu^i(X_t)]$ for i=1,2. The comparison uses $\ell(\pi,\nu)=\max_{i\in\{1,2\}}\mathbb E_\nu R_i(T)$.

Take the expectation of each signed coordinate regret first and then the maximum over the two coordinates. This is not $\mathbb E\max_iR_i(T)$, a positive-part regret, a weighted sum, or a high-probability threshold. Secondary signed regret may be negative; primary regret is nonnegative.
